confidenceRationale: Option C aligns with both the pragmatic constraints identified and the existing momentum of the auto-memory system. It avoids introducing unproven external dependencies (OmniMem maturity is unknown) while delivering 80% of the value.

architecturalAssessment.rationale: The three-level architecture (raw sessions → summaries → consolidated trusted memory) is a well-established pattern in information management systems. It mirrors how knowledge management systems handle the distinction between raw data, processed information, and actionable knowledge. The proposed metadata schema (status/scope/project/confidence/source) is minimal and sufficient. The key principle of avoiding toxic memory is correctly identified as the central risk.
strengths: Explicit lifecycle states prevent the single biggest risk: stale-as-authoritative
Scope separation (personal/project/client/experiment) maps correctly to Luca's multi-context workload
The three-level hierarchy provides natural pruning boundaries — raw sessions can be dropped without losing consolidated knowledge
Already has an existing foundation to build on (auto-memory system)
weaknesses: Level 1 (raw session history) is already partially covered by ~/.claude/sessions/ — potential duplication
The 'codebase memory / knowledge graph' is scope creep that risks delaying MVP
OmniMem is an unknown quantity — no clear track record for Claude Code specifically

OmniMem.rationale: OmniMem's claimed features (contradiction detection, memory scoring, lifecycle management) are exactly what's needed, but it is an external dependency with unclear maturity for Claude Code. Evaluate in Phase 3 once the manual process has stabilised. If it works, it becomes the automation layer for Phase 4. Do not adopt in MVP.

qmdSessions.rationale: Converting JSONL transcripts to searchable Markdown is genuinely useful for session retrieval but is not a day-1 requirement. Raw sessions already exist in ~/.claude/sessions/. Add in Phase 2 once the consolidated memory layer is established and the search need is confirmed.

BMADStyle.rationale: Luca already uses BMAD patterns in his registry. Using BMAD methodology principles (artifact-first, explicit state, decision logs, gates) as the structural discipline for the memory system itself is the correct approach. Not a tool, but the methodological backbone. It should govern when memories are created, when they are promoted from draft to active, and when they are deprecated.

CodebaseMemory.rationale: Structural codebase memory (modules, dependencies, ADRs) is valuable for large refactoring projects but is already partially served by the indexing-supervisor agent in the registry. Defer to Phase 5 and evaluate whether the indexing-supervisor's .indexing-kb/ output already covers this need.

MemoryMCP.rationale: MCP memory server (e.g., sqlite-based or filesystem MCP) is the correct mechanism for Phase 3 — it gives Claude Code a native read/write interface to the memory layer without requiring custom tooling. This should be evaluated in Phase 3 alongside OmniMem.

minimumViableImplementation.description: Formalise the existing auto-memory system with lifecycle rules and add a personal global memory layer
steps: 1. Create ~/.claude/memory/personal/ with an initial PERSONAL-MEMORY.md index
2. Write 5-10 consolidated memories from existing sessions (patterns, anti-patterns, preferences already observed)
3. Add lifecycle rules to global CLAUDE.md: when to search, when to update, how to handle stale, cross-project rules
4. Formalise per-project MEMORY.md convention: require status/scope/confidence fields on every entry
5. Create /memory-review slash command: lists all active memories by last_verified date, flags overdue for review
minimumViableImplementation.estimatedEffort: 4-6 hours for initial setup; 10-15 minutes per session for maintenance

rules: Every memory entry has status: active|superseded|deprecated|draft — only 'active' is retrieved by default
Every memory entry has last_verified date — entries older than 60 days (personal) or 30 days (project) are auto-flagged as 'needs-review' in retrieval context
Experiment scope entries are NEVER retrieved as decisions — they are explicitly tagged and excluded from the active decision pool
Cross-project contamination: project-scoped memories are only retrieved when Claude is operating in that project context (CLAUDE.md path-based scoping)
When a contradiction is detected between two active memories, both are immediately set to 'draft' pending manual review — never auto-resolve
Low-confidence memories are retrieved with an explicit warning prefix: [LOW CONFIDENCE — verify before applying]
